international.title: Israeli justice system at tipping point as judges call for end to Netanyahu trial
international.summary: Dropping of corruption charges against PM after highly unusual intervention could set damaging precedent The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision. The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account. Continue reading...
